mentions.excerpt: Moses Sternstein, writing the Charts of the Week series at a16z, supplies evidence that demand has not yet broken.
Moses Sternstein’s charts at a16z show data centers accounting for about 60% of private non-residential building in New Mexico and Wyoming.
Moses Sternstein puts paid consumer AI adoption at roughly 3% in the first quarter.

sides.claim: Hyperscalers have poured free cashflow and debt into computational infrastructure to meet AI's demands, creating a generational run in semiconductors where demand has outpaced supply.

AI usage is highly concentrated among power users and top-decile enterprises, which have increased token output by more than 17 times since April 2025, creating an approximately 8-fold gap between typical and top-decile enterprises, and a gap…
The data suggests that, for now, the story is 'App-Slop': AI has produced many more apps, but they are not successful apps in any meaningful sense.
Paid consumer AI adoption remains quite low even though it is growing, per Consumer Edge data showing roughly 3% adoption as of Q1, with younger people adopting at about 4x the rate of older people.
